title: 2 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who reigned in Judah in the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Amaziah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:1 states that Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah reigned in the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

questions.question: How old was Amaziah when he began to reign, and how long did he reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: 25 years old, reigned 29 years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:2 tells us Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the name of Amaziah's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoaddan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:2 mentions Amaziah's mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

questions.question: How did Amaziah's actions compare to those of his father Joash and David?
options: Did right in the sight of the LORD, but not like David; did according to Joash
Did evil in the sight of the LORD, unlike both David and Joash
Did exactly like David but not like Joash
Did better than both David and Joash
questions.correctAnswer: Did right in the sight of the LORD, but not like David; did according to Joash
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:3 states Amaziah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father; he did according to all things as Joash his father did.

questions.question: Did Amaziah remove the high places where people sacrificed and burnt incense?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:4 says the high places were not taken away and people still sacrificed and burnt incense there.

questions.question: What did Amaziah do as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in his hand?
options: Slew his servants who had slain his father
questions.correctAnswer: Slew his servants who had slain his father
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:5 states that Amaziah slew his servants who had slain the king his father as soon as his kingdom was confirmed.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah also killed the children of the murderers of his father.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:6 explains Amaziah did not kill the children of the murderers, following the law of Moses that children should not be put to death for their fathers' sins.

questions.question: How many Edomites did Amaziah kill in the valley of salt?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:7 records that Amaziah slew ten thousand Edomites in the valley of salt.

questions.question: What city did Amaziah capture and rename Joktheel?
questions.correctAnswer: Selah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:7 states Amaziah took Selah by war and called its name Joktheel.

questions.question: To whom did Amaziah send messengers inviting to 'look one another in the face'?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoash king of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:8 states Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, king of Israel, inviting him to meet face to face.

questions.question: What analogy did Jehoash use to warn Amaziah against going to war with Israel?
options: The thistle and the cedar in Lebanon
The lion and the lamb in the field
The wolf and the sheep in the fold
The eagle and the dove in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: The thistle and the cedar in Lebanon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:9 records Jehoash's message comparing Amaziah to a thistle asking to marry the cedar's daughter, but a wild beast trod the thistle down.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoash advised Amaziah to continue his war against Israel to glory.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:10 shows Jehoash telling Amaziah to glory in his victory over Edom and stay home rather than meddle to his own hurt.

questions.question: What happened when Amaziah ignored Jehoash's advice and they met in battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah was defeated and fled
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:12 states Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to their tents.

questions.question: What came first in 2 Kings 14: Amaziah killing his father's murderers or sending messengers to Jehoash?
questions.correctAnswer: Killing his father's murderers
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:5 describes Amaziah killing his father's murderers before sending messengers to Jehoash in 2 Kings 14:8.

questions.question: True or False: The high places were completely removed during Amaziah's reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:4 explicitly states the high places were not taken away during Amaziah's reign.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the result when Amaziah refused to heed Jehoash's warning and they faced each other in battle at Bethshemesh?
options: Amaziah defeated Israel and captured Jehoash
Judah was put to the worse before Israel and fled every man to their tents
They made peace and formed an alliance
questions.correctAnswer: Judah was put to the worse before Israel and fled every man to their tents
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:11 describes Amaziah's refusal to listen to Jehoash's warning, leading to the battle at Bethshemesh where 2 Kings 14:12 states Judah was defeated and fled. This shows the consequence of ignoring wise counsel.

questions.question: How did Jehoash king of Israel demonstrate his victory over Amaziah king of Judah after their battle?
options: He captured Amaziah and made him a prisoner for life
He broke down the wall of Jerusalem and took treasures and hostages
He executed all the leaders of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He broke down the wall of Jerusalem and took treasures and hostages
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 14:13-14, Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem from gate of Ephraim to the corner gate and took all gold, silver, vessels from the house of the LORD and king’s treasures, along with hostages, demonstrating total victory.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 14:15 imply about the recording of the kings' deeds and why is this significant for believers?
options: It shows that only good deeds are recorded
It confirms that detailed records of kings’ acts and might are preserved for learning
It states that only the king’s failures are recorded
It suggests the records were lost and unavailable
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms that detailed records of kings’ acts and might are preserved for learning
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:15 mentions the book of chronicles recording Jehoash’s deeds and might, teaching believers the importance of documenting life events and learning from history (see also 2 Kings 14:18).

questions.question: How does the account of Amaziah's death in 2 Kings 14:19-20 teach about the consequences of leadership failure?
options: He died peacefully in old age
He was betrayed by a conspiracy, fled, but was killed, showing that failure to lead rightly can bring violent ends
He was honored by all and buried with great ceremony
He abdicated and lived in exile
questions.correctAnswer: He was betrayed by a conspiracy, fled, but was killed, showing that failure to lead rightly can bring violent ends
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 describe a conspiracy against Amaziah, his flight, and murder, demonstrating that poor leadership and disobedience can lead to downfall and death, a warning for leaders to act with integrity and humility.

questions.question: What lesson about faithfulness and God’s providence can be learned from Jeroboam son of Joash’s reign as described in 2 Kings 14:23-27?
options: God abandons Israel completely when they sin
Despite evil deeds, God did not blot out Israel's name but saved them through Jeroboam
Jeroboam was a perfect king who obeyed all God's commands
Israel conquered all neighboring nations without struggle
questions.correctAnswer: Despite evil deeds, God did not blot out Israel's name but saved them through Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:24-27 shows that although Jeroboam did evil, God preserved Israel and saved them through him, teaching that God's mercy can work even through imperfect leaders.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah executed the children of his father's murderers according to the law of Moses.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:6 explicitly states Amaziah slew the murderers but spared their children, following the Mosaic law that fathers and children should not be punished for each other's sins.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 14:7 reveal about Amaziah’s military success and how might this reflect God’s blessing?
options: He lost the battle and fled
He slew 10,000 Edomites and took Selah, renaming it Joktheel
He made peace with Edom without fighting
He was defeated by Edom and captured
questions.correctAnswer: He slew 10,000 Edomites and took Selah, renaming it Joktheel
questions.explanation: Verse 7 recounts Amaziah’s victory over Edom, showing a tangible military success that can be seen as a blessing following his initial obedience to the LORD.

questions.question: How does the interaction between Amaziah and Jehoash in 2 Kings 14:8-10 teach about humility and pride?
options: Jehoash humbly asked for peace and respect
Jehoash warned Amaziah not to be prideful after his victory over Edom, comparing him to a thistle challenged by a cedar
Amaziah was praised for his humility
Jehoash encouraged Amaziah to attack Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoash warned Amaziah not to be prideful after his victory over Edom, comparing him to a thistle challenged by a cedar
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 use the metaphor of the thistle and cedar to caution Amaziah against pride after his success, illustrating the biblical virtue of humility before God and others.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 14:17 teach about Amaziah’s life after the death of Jehoash of Israel?
options: Amaziah reigned only a few months after Jehoash’s death
Amaziah lived fifteen years after Jehoash’s death
questions.correctAnswer: Amaziah lived fifteen years after Jehoash’s death
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states Amaziah lived fifteen years after Jehoash’s death, showing continuity of his reign despite the defeat and political turmoil.

questions.question: What practical Christian lesson about forgiveness and justice can be drawn from Amaziah’s treatment of his father’s murderers and their children in 2 Kings 14:5-6?
options: He took revenge on both murderers and their children
He showed justice by punishing the guilty but spared the innocent children, following God's law
He killed the children but spared the murderers
questions.correctAnswer: He showed justice by punishing the guilty but spared the innocent children, following God's law
questions.explanation: These verses teach believers to balance justice with mercy, punishing wrongdoing but not extending punishment to innocent parties, reflecting God's law.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 14:21-22, what did Azariah do after becoming king of Judah?
options: He built Elath and restored it to Judah
He destroyed the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He built Elath and restored it to Judah
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 show Azariah’s efforts in rebuilding and restoring territory, teaching about faithful stewardship and restoration after crisis.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoash of Israel was buried in Jerusalem with the kings of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:16 states Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, not in Jerusalem where Judah's kings were buried.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 14:23-25 reveal about Jeroboam son of Joash’s military achievements and God’s provision?
options: He lost all territories to Judah
He restored Israel’s borders from Hamath to the sea of the plain, fulfilling the prophecy of Jonah
He made peace treaties with all neighbors without fighting
He ignored the prophets and expanded by his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: He restored Israel’s borders from Hamath to the sea of the plain, fulfilling the prophecy of Jonah
questions.explanation: These verses show Jeroboam’s success in recovering territory as foretold by the prophet Jonah, demonstrating God’s providential control over Israel’s history.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 14:28-29, Jeroboam was succeeded by his son Zachariah as king of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 29 confirms Jeroboam slept with his fathers and his son Zachariah reigned in his place, showing the dynastic succession.

questions.question: In the context of 2 Kings 14, how does Amaziah’s failure to heed advice (verses 8-11) illustrate a biblical principle for believers today?
options: Ignoring wise counsel can lead to unnecessary conflict and defeat
Ignoring advice always leads to blessings
Pride is not mentioned as a problem
Believers should always challenge their enemies regardless
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring wise counsel can lead to unnecessary conflict and defeat
questions.explanation: Verses 8-11 show Amaziah’s refusal to listen to Jehoash’s warning led to his defeat, teaching believers the importance of humility and heeding godly counsel.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who was made king of Judah at the age of sixteen after Amaziah?
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:21 states that the people of Judah made Azariah, who was sixteen years old, king instead of his father Amaziah.

questions.question: What city did Azariah restore to Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Elath
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 14:22, Azariah built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king died.

questions.question: How long did Jeroboam the son of Joash reign in Samaria?
questions.correctAnswer: 41 years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:23 tells us Jeroboam son of Joash reigned forty and one years in Samaria.

questions.question: What is said about Jeroboam's behavior in the sight of the LORD?
options: He did evil and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
He did right as David did
He was righteous and followed the law fully
He was neutral in his reign
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:24 states Jeroboam did evil and did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 14, which prophet's word did Jeroboam fulfill by restoring Israel's borders?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah the son of Amittai
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:25 mentions Jeroboam restored the coast of Israel according to the word of the LORD spoken through Jonah the son of Amittai.

questions.question: What was the condition of Israel at the time the LORD saw their affliction?
options: Very bitter with no shut up, left, or helper
questions.correctAnswer: Very bitter with no shut up, left, or helper
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:26 describes Israel's affliction as very bitter, without anyone shut up, left, or a helper.

questions.question: What did the LORD decide regarding the name of Israel under heaven?
options: He would not blot it out but saved them by Jeroboam
He would blot it out immediately
He gave Israel a new name
questions.correctAnswer: He would not blot it out but saved them by Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:27 states the LORD did not blot out Israel's name but saved them by Jeroboam son of Joash.

questions.question: What military achievements of Jeroboam are recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
options: His wars and recovery of Damascus and Hamath
questions.correctAnswer: His wars and recovery of Damascus and Hamath
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:28 notes Jeroboam's acts, might, wars, and recovery of Damascus and Hamath are written in the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

questions.question: Who reigned after Jeroboam died?
questions.correctAnswer: Zachariah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:29 states that after Jeroboam slept with his fathers, Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage is directly connected with Jeroboam's restoration of Israel's borders as prophesied in 2 Kings 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah 1:1-2
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:25 references Jonah the son of Amittai's prophecy, which begins in Jonah 1:1-2, linking the restoration of Israel's borders with Jonah's mission.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the name 'Azariah' as used for the king of Judah in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Yahweh has helped
questions.explanation: The name 'Azariah' (עֲזַרְיָה) means 'Yahweh has helped,' reflecting divine assistance, relevant to 2 Kings 14:21 where Azariah becomes king.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in 2 Kings 14:9-10, where Jehoash of Israel uses the analogy of a thistle and cedar to warn Amaziah?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:9-10 employs a parable comparing the thistle and cedar to convey a moral warning, a storytelling device used to illustrate Amaziah's folly.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 14:24, Jeroboam son of Joash departed from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:24 explicitly states Jeroboam son of Joash did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, so the statement is False.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Kings 14:27 shows that despite Israel's affliction, the LORD chose to preserve their name under heaven through Jeroboam son of Joash.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:27 confirms the LORD did not blot out Israel's name but saved them by Jeroboam son of Joash, so the statement is True.

questions.question: Which historical city did Jeroboam recover that previously belonged to Judah, according to 2 Kings 14:28?
questions.correctAnswer: Damascus
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:28 records that Jeroboam recovered Damascus, which had belonged to Judah, as part of his military campaigns.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle about individual responsibility before God is taught in Amaziah's actions toward his father's murderers and their children?
options: Children bear the punishment for their parents' sins
Every man shall be put to death for his own sin
All family members share equally in judgment
The king can punish whom he wishes regardless of law
questions.correctAnswer: Every man shall be put to death for his own sin
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:5-6 teaches that Amaziah slew the murderers of his father but spared their children, following the Mosaic law that fathers are not put to death for children nor children for fathers, but each for their own sin. This highlights personal responsibility before God (see also Ezekiel 18:20).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's decision not to blot out Israel despite their affliction and sinfulness during Jeroboam's reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:26-27 shows that although Israel was greatly afflicted and sinful, the LORD chose not to blot out their name but saved them by Jeroboam’s hand. This reveals God's mercy in judgment (cf. Exodus 34:6).

questions.question: What theological insight about human pride and divine warning is conveyed through Jehoash's message to Amaziah comparing a thistle and a cedar in Lebanon?
options: Pride leads to destruction and God warns to avoid overreaching
God favors the proud in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to destruction and God warns to avoid overreaching
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:9-10 uses the metaphor of a thistle and cedar to warn Amaziah that his pride after victory over Edom would lead to his downfall if he meddled further. This reflects the biblical principle that God opposes the proud (Proverbs 16:18).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 14:3-4, how does Amaziah's religious practice reflect the tension between covenant faithfulness and syncretism?
options: He fully removed high places and worshiped only Yahweh
He did right in God's sight but allowed high place worship to continue
He rejected David's example and embraced pagan gods
He abolished all forms of sacrifices and incense
questions.correctAnswer: He did right in God's sight but allowed high place worship to continue
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 state Amaziah did right according to Joash's ways but did not remove high places where people sacrificed. This shows partial covenant faithfulness marred by tolerated syncretism (cf. 1 Kings 15:14).

questions.question: What does the restoration of the border from Hamath to the sea of the plain by Jeroboam son of Joash signify in terms of God's providential preservation of Israel?
options: Israel lost all its territories permanently
God restored Israel’s borders as part of His salvific plan
The borders were irrelevant to Israel's identity
questions.correctAnswer: God restored Israel’s borders as part of His salvific plan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:25-27 reveals God’s providential hand in restoring Israel’s territory through Jeroboam, preserving the nation despite past sins and afflictions. This fits the biblical theme of covenant faithfulness and restoration (Jeremiah 30:3).

questions.question: How does the account of Amaziah’s death and conspiracy against him illustrate the biblical doctrine of human sinfulness and divine judgment?
options: Sin leads to downfall and God's judgment often works through human agency
God protects all kings from harm
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to downfall and God's judgment often works through human agency
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 14:19-20 narrates a conspiracy causing Amaziah to flee and be killed, showing how human sin and rebellion result in judgment often enacted by other humans as divine instruments (cf. Psalm 7:14-16).

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about kingship and covenant faithfulness emerges from comparing Amaziah’s reign (verses 1-3) and Jeroboam’s reign (verses 23-24)?
options: Both kings perfectly kept the covenant
Amaziah did right but imperfectly; Jeroboam did evil continuing ancestral sins
Neither king had any impact on Israel or Judah
Jeroboam was righteous, Amaziah was wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Amaziah did right but imperfectly; Jeroboam did evil continuing ancestral sins
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show Amaziah did right in the LORD's sight though not like David, while verses 23-24 state Jeroboam did evil, perpetuating sin. This illustrates the biblical theme of covenant obedience and consequences of sin in kingship (cf. Deuteronomy 17:18-20).

questions.question: In light of 2 Kings 14:7, what does Amaziah’s military victory over Edom and renaming of Selah to Joktheel typologically indicate about God’s providence and sovereignty?
options: God's providence is irrelevant in warfare
God sovereignly grants victory and redefines places to signify His purposes
Renaming places was a pagan practice without theological meaning
Military success depends solely on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly grants victory and redefines places to signify His purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows Amaziah’s victory and renaming Selah to Joktheel, indicating God’s sovereign control over history and places, foreshadowing how God redefines human events for His glory (cf. Genesis 32:28).

questions.question: What does the destruction of the wall of Jerusalem by Jehoash in 2 Kings 14:13 teach about God's judgment mediated through human instruments?
options: God never uses foreign kings for judgment
God often uses human agents, even enemies, to execute judgment on His people
Only divine angels enact God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God often uses human agents, even enemies, to execute judgment on His people
questions.explanation: Verse 13 describes Jehoash breaking Jerusalem’s wall after defeating Amaziah, exemplifying how God uses surrounding nations to discipline Israel and Judah when they are unfaithful (cf. Isaiah 10:5-6).

questions.question: How does Amaziah’s partial obedience (2 Kings 14:3-4) reflect the biblical doctrine of sanctification and human imperfection?
options: Sanctification is immediate and perfect in this life
Believers can do right yet still struggle with sin and compromise
Partial obedience is equal to full obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Believers can do right yet still struggle with sin and compromise
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 indicate Amaziah did right in the LORD’s sight but did not remove high places, showing sanctification is a progressive, imperfect process where believers still wrestle with sin (cf. Romans 7:15-20).

questions.question: How does Jeroboam’s reign fulfilling the prophecy given by Jonah (2 Kings 14:25) demonstrate the interplay between prophecy and divine sovereignty in biblical theology?
options: God sovereignly fulfills His prophetic word through history
Prophecy has no real influence on events
Jonah’s prophecy was unrelated to Jeroboam’s reign
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly fulfills His prophetic word through history
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states Jeroboam restored Israel’s borders as prophesied by Jonah, showing how God’s sovereign plan unfolds through prophetic revelation and historical fulfillment (cf. Isaiah 55:11).

questions.question: What do the contrasting outcomes of Amaziah’s and Jehoash’s confrontations (2 Kings 14:11-14) reveal about divine justice and human pride?
options: Pride leads to downfall and defeats authorized by God
Human pride is rewarded by God
Divine justice is unrelated to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to downfall and defeats authorized by God
questions.explanation: Verses 11-14 narrate Amaziah’s pride leading to defeat by Jehoash, who then plunders Jerusalem. This illustrates the biblical principle that God humbles the proud and executes justice through human events (cf. Proverbs 16:18).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's justice is inconsistent because kings like Amaziah who sinned still reigned long and prospered. What does 2 Kings 14:2-3 and 14:17 teach about divine justice and mercy in the context of covenant leadership?
options: God combines justice and mercy, allowing partial obedience and consequences
Kings are exempt from divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God combines justice and mercy, allowing partial obedience and consequences
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 record Amaziah doing right yet imperfectly, reigning 29 years, and verse 17 shows he lived 15 years after Jehoash’s death. This reflects God's balanced justice and mercy—leaders may prosper despite sin but face consequences, consistent with biblical teaching (cf. Romans 2:4-5).

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from the combined narrative of Amaziah’s partial obedience (2 Kings 14:3-4), Jehoash’s judgment (2 Kings 14:13-14), and Jeroboam’s evil reign (2 Kings 14:24)?
options: God tolerates all sin without consequence
God’s holiness demands judgment on sin, while partial obedience delays but does not remove consequences
Kings are free from God’s law
Judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to behavior
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands judgment on sin, while partial obedience delays but does not remove consequences
questions.explanation: These passages together show Amaziah’s partial obedience, Jehoash’s punishment of Judah, and Jeroboam’s evil reign resulting in judgment, teaching that God's holiness requires judgment on sin though mercy may temper timing (cf. Hebrews 12:6).

questions.question: What does the installation of Azariah as king at age sixteen after Amaziah’s death (2 Kings 14:21) reveal about God's providential care for covenant continuity despite human failure?
options: God abandons His covenant people after a king’s death
God providentially preserves David’s line to continue His promises
Kingship is irrelevant to God’s plan
Only old kings can lead God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially preserves David’s line to continue His promises
questions.explanation: Verse 21 shows the people made Azariah king after Amaziah, reflecting God's providential preservation of the Davidic covenant line despite human sin and turmoil (cf. 2 Samuel 7:12-16).
